title: Wire a real no-emit typecheck into a TypeScript Bun project's check path

facts.note: Tree contains at least one .ts/.tsx source.
Scope requires a package.json AND at least one .ts/.tsx source; tsconfig, dependencies and scripts are read from these files.
Read at the consumer repository root.
Declared addition: marker files used to identify the tree as a Bun project; the source says only 'Bun project'.
Any work on or validation of the project; standing obligation, not restricted to diffs touching config.
Consumer vs convention-hub/package-repository classification; the hub is excluded. Needs a repository-classification observer.

Validator result: missing typechecker dependency, missing tsconfig, no no-emit typecheck script, or demonstrably-not-strict tsconfig. Evaluated on every in-scope consumer project whether or not the current task edited these files.

fires: Any work on or validation of a consumer Bun project with package.json and .ts/.tsx sources, regardless of whether the current change touches dependencies, tsconfig or scripts.
A Bun TypeScript project has no TypeScript (or native preview such as tsgo) in dependencies/devDependencies.
A Bun TypeScript project has no tsconfig.json.
A Bun TypeScript project has TypeScript and a tsconfig.json, but no script runs a no-emit typecheck.
A Bun TypeScript project's tsconfig.json that extends no base config sets "strict": false, or enables no strict-family flag.
doesNotFire: A JS-only Bun app with no .ts/.tsx sources.
Strictness of a tsconfig that extends a base config (never reported; the other requirements still apply).
The convention hub/package repository whose .ts files are deliberately-wrong fixtures.

The script (HOW) requirement only: a project using any recognised no-emit checker (tsc --noEmit, tsgo --noEmit, vue-tsc, svelte-check, astro check, tsc --build) in any script, or a script named typecheck / check-types / types, satisfies that requirement — the rule still fires if the TypeScript dependency or tsconfig.json is missing or the tsconfig is demonstrably not strict.

given: A consumer Bun project with a package.json and at least one .ts/.tsx source
when: the project is worked on or validated (standing obligation)
then: The project has TypeScript (or a native preview such as tsgo) as a dependency, a tsconfig.json, and a no-emit typecheck script wired into its check path.
prefer: A script (e.g. `typecheck`) running a recognised no-emit checker such as `tsc --noEmit` or `tsgo --noEmit`, invoked by the developer/CI check scripts.

During GREEN: reuse the existing typechecker and strict config (which checker is the project's choice); add only the minimal missing dependency, config or script; fix type errors from the current behavior instead of weakening compiler options.
avoid: A typecheck no developer/CI script invokes.
Relying on Bun: it strips types and bundles no tsc.
"strict": false, or no strict-family flag (e.g. `strict`, `noImplicitAny`), in a tsconfig extending no base.
Disabling strict checks or adding blanket ignores.
Replacing the typechecker without necessity, or migrating unrelated configuration while establishing the check.
unless: Strictness only: a tsconfig that extends a base is never reported.
The convention hub is never scanned; its .ts files are fixtures.
why: Bun strips types and ships no typechecker, so without a wired, actually run typecheck a Bun stack is by default less type-safe than a tsc-based one; shape detectors can't confirm code conforms to its types.
evidence: package.json lists typescript (or a native preview such as tsgo) in dependencies or devDependencies, and a tsconfig.json exists.
Some script runs a recognised no-emit typechecker, or is named typecheck / check-types / types, and is part of the scripts a developer or CI runs to validate the project.
The no-emit typecheck succeeds through the repository's normal check path.
tsconfig.json is not demonstrably non-strict (or extends a base config).
verifier_detail: Scope: only trees that are genuinely TypeScript projects — a package.json AND at least one .ts/.tsx source. JS-only Bun apps carry no obligation at all.

typechecker = a tool that verifies types without emitting output. Recognised: `tsc --noEmit`, `tsgo --noEmit`, `vue-tsc`, `svelte-check`, `astro check`, `tsc --build`. Any of them in any script satisfies HOW; so does a script simply named `typecheck` / `check-types` / `types`. The obligation is that types ARE checked; WHICH checker is the project's business.
check_path = the scripts a developer or CI runs to validate the project; a typecheck that exists but is never invoked is not wired in — it is a tool sitting beside the build, not part of it.

demonstrably_not_strict = tsconfig.json sets `"strict": false` outright, OR enables no flag of the strict family AND extends no base config. STRICTNESS is reported only when demonstrably off. A tsconfig that `extends` anything is NOT judged: the detector cannot resolve the base, and reporting what it cannot see would be a false positive (a rule that reports what it cannot see is worse than one that stays quiet).
Deliberately unforced in four ways (SCOPE, HOW, WHERE, STRICTNESS): the rule states a norm, not a blessed incantation.

Complementary, not overlapping, with the other Bun detectors, and that distinction is the reason the rule exists: every detector in this stack is regex-over-source and verifies SHAPE. E.g. coder.bun.interlocking-resolution-model-exists confirms an `InterlockingResolution` declaring its eight fields is present, but cannot confirm that what `resolveTrain` actually returns conforms to it — only a typechecker can, and only if one is actually run.

Bun executes .ts by STRIPPING types; it ships `bun test`, `bun install`, `bun build`, `Bun.serve` and a TS/JSX transpiler, but no typechecker (no bundled `tsc`); it transpiles and never checks, so `resolveTrain()` can return something structurally wrong and Bun will run it happily.

Applies to the consumer repository, never the hub. The hub is a package repository with no Bun application; its detectors are `.mjs` and its `.ts` files are deliberately-wrong fixtures that must NOT typecheck (e.g. `fixtures/dirty/interlocking_resolution_model/...` exists precisely to be malformed). The hub is never scanned by this rule.
audit: Summary framing: 'Bun's own gap, stated as a convention.'
Source name: 'A TypeScript Bun project actually typechecks its types'

splitSuggestion.then: A Bun TypeScript project's tsconfig.json is not demonstrably non-strict (not "strict": false, and not lacking every strict-family flag while extending no base).

strict: the extension fails on every finding; it has no advisory mode and no ratchet baseline.
